text: The DiffTRe authors see the main obstacle in bottom-up training of neural network potentials as the limited availability of highly precise and sufficiently broad datasets, which becomes intractable for larger systems where quantum calculations are too costly [W3168247670#003]. The SchNet C20 model relied on this approach: its reference data came from classical MD run with DFT (PBE+vdW-TS) [W2778051509#019]. Instead, DiffTRe uses a top-down approach that trains on experimental data. Examples include a DimeNet++ model for diamond fitted to its experimental stiffness tensor, and a coarse-grained water model fitted to pressure and radial and angular distribution functions [W3168247670#003].
